dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: jalasyevormayo vahner jvālābhaṅgyaḥ prabhā raveḥ | mamaiva bhairavasyaitā viśvabhaṅgyo vibheditāḥ ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: 'As waves arise from water, flickering flames from fire and rays from the sun, so these varied waves of the universe arise, differentiated, from me, Bhairava.'
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: the dhāraṇā of the second phase of recognition: having recognised the individual as Śiva (verse 109), one recognises that the glory of manifestation is one's own, the identity of the universe with the Self. Wallis: 'the waves arise from me'.
dharana.technique_name: Waves from Water: The World Arising from Me
dharana.instruction: See sights, sounds and thoughts as waves rising from your own awareness, like waves from water.

checked_against: The Mystery Within (2019), Session Two list: 'Dharana 86' = verse 110 (agrees with Singh)
Wallis concordance: verse 110 = 'The waves arise from me (Y85 ~ B2)' (verse text and technique match)
GRETIL, Wallis and Pradīpaka: Sanskrit of verse 110 compared
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: verse 110: The waves arise from me (Y85 ~ B2)
numbering_variants.mystery_within_parallel: The parallel-translations section of The Mystery Within labels verse 110 'Dharana 87', because from verse 106 on it gives every verse its own number (106 = 83 … 137 = 114). Singh and the same book's Session Two list put this at dhāraṇā 86. Not followed.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 110 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is three images, waves, flames and rays, each showing many forms rising from one source, and the world rising from oneself in the same way.
geometry.svg_hint: waves rising from a line of water, flames from a single fire, rays from a sun
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Waves of the world
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: the world stops looking like something outside and is seen as rising from one's own awareness, like waves from water. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Turn attention toward what the verse names, and let everything else stay in the background
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The images of waves from water, flames from fire, rays from the sun
attention.secondary: Seeing the world arise from one's own awareness in the same way

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: 'As waves arise from water, flickering flames from fire and rays from the sun, so these varied waves of the universe arise, differentiated, from me, Bhairava.'
adiyogi.method_summary: Picture waves rising from water, flames from fire, rays from the sun: many forms, one source. Then look at the world (sounds, sights, thoughts) as waves rising from your own awareness. Rest as the water.

honesty.disclosure: Door 086 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 86 (verse 110) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 086 is dharana 86, verse 110. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
New door researched on 2026-10-06 on branch research/vbt-houses-2-7; awaiting guardian review.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. A contemplation of awareness, not a claim of personal control over events. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
